'''Alexis Ajinça''' ({{IPA|fr|alɛksi aʒɛ̃sa}}; born 6 May 1988) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played seven seasons in the league for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Toronto Raptors]] and [[New Orleans Pelicans]].

==Early life==
Ajinça was a promising [[BMX]] rider during his childhood and routinely won racing competitions for his age group in France.<ref name=twt>{{cite web |title=Bobcats impressed with Ajinca |url=https://restorationnewsmedia.com/articles/wilsontimes/bobcats-impressed-with-ajinca/ |website=The Wilson Times |access-date=30 November 2023 |date=10 July 2008}}</ref> He started playing basketball at age of 12 because he thought that it would help him improve his bike jumps.<ref name=twt /> Ajinça gave up BMX riding when he blossomed in basketball.<ref name=twt />

==Professional career==
===Early years (2006–2008)===
After attending France's [[INSEP]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Alexis-Ajinca-534/|title=Alexis Ajinca|work=draftexpress.com|access-date=7 December 2017|archive-date=2 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002045057/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Alexis-Ajinca-534/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ajinça played for [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|Pau-Orthez]] during the 2006–07 season. He joined [[Hyères-Toulon Var Basket|Hyères-Toulon]] for the 2007–08 season and averaged 5.0 points and 3.1 rebounds per game.<ref name=twt />

===Charlotte Bobcats (2008–2010)===
Ajinça was selected with the 20th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/draft_pick_080626.html|title=Bobcats Select Augustin, Ajinca and Weaver in 2008 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=26 June 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080630073156/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/draft_pick_080626.html|archive-date=30 June 2008}}</ref> The Bobcats wanted to select a [[Big man (basketball)|big man]] after selecting guard [[D. J. Augustin]] earlier in the draft and believed that Ajinça possessed the most potential of players available.<ref name=twt />

During his rookie season, he spent time with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. During his second season with Charlotte, he spent time with the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{fact|date=April 2026}}

===Dallas Mavericks (2010–2011)===
On 13 July 2010, Ajinça was traded, along with [[Tyson Chandler]], to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Erick Dampier]], [[Eduardo Nájera]], [[Matt Carroll (basketball)|Matt Carroll]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5377055|title=Mavs get Chandler from Bobcats|work=ESPN|date=14 July 2020|access-date=27 December 2022|last=Stein|first=Marc}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2011)===
On 24 January 2011, Ajinça was traded, along with a future second-round draft pick and cash considerations, to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Georgios Printezis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/20110124/9929/raptors-acquire-ajinca-draft-pick-and-cash-considerations-dallas|title=Raptors Acquire Ajinca, Draft Pick And Cash Considerations From Dallas|work=NBA.com|date=24 January 2011|access-date=24 January 2011}}</ref>

===Return to France (2011–2013)===
On 2 November 2011, Ajinça joined [[Paris-Levallois Basket|Paris-Levallois]] for a one-week tryout.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/88838/paris-levallois-announced-the-arrival-for-a-1-week-tryout-of-ajinca.html|title=Paris-Levallois announced the arrival for a 1-week tryout of Ajinca|work=Sportando.com|date=2 November 2011|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> He left the team on 8 November<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/88878/alexis-ajinca-leaves-paris-levallois.html|title=Alexis Ajinca leaves Paris-Levallois|work=Sportando.com|date=8 November 2011|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> and joined [[Hyères-Toulon Var Basket|Hyères-Toulon]] two days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/88892/alexis-ajinca-returns-to-hyeres-toulon.html|title=Alexis Ajinca returns to Hyeres-Toulon|work=Sportando.com|date=10 November 2011|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> He appeared in just two games with Hyères-Toulon before parting ways with the team.

After failing to make a return to the NBA following the conclusion of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/89508/sig-strasbourg-to-sign-alexis-ajinca.html|title=SIG Strasbourg to sign Alexis Ajinca?|work=Sportando.com|date=26 December 2011|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> Ajinça returned to France and signed with [[SIG Strasbourg]] on 29 December 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/89542/sig-strasbourg-signs-big-man-alexis-ajinca.html|title=SIG Strasbourg signs big man Alexis Ajinca|work=Sportando.com|date=29 December 2011|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 13 August 2012, he re-signed with Strasbourg for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/94446/sig-strasbourg-keeps-alexis-ajinca.html|title=SIG Strasbourg keeps Alexis Ajinca|work=Sportando.com|date=13 August 2012|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 6 August 2013, he re-signed with Strasbourg for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/104662/alexis-ajinca-re-signs-with-sig-strasbourg.html|title=Alexis Ajinca re-signs with SIG Strasbourg|work=Sportando.com|date=6 August 2013|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 18 December 2013, he left Strasbourg to return to the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/109399/alexis-ajinca-leaves-sig-strasbourg-to-join-new-orleans-pelicans.html|title=Alexis Ajinca leaves SIG Strasbourg to join New Orleans Pelicans|work=Sportando.com|date=18 December 2013|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2018)===
On 20 December 2013, Ajinça signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-center-alexis-ajinca/|title=PELICANS SIGN AJINCA|work=NBA.com|date=20 December 2013|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 9 July 2015, he re-signed with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-re-sign-ajinca-asik-and-cunningham|title=Pelicans Re-Sign Ajinca, Asik and Cunningham|work=NBA.com|date=9 July 2015|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> On 8 April 2016, he recorded career highs with 28 points and 15 rebounds in a 110–102 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/LALNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Pelicans beat Lakers, Kobe Bryant 110-102|work=NBA.com|date=8 April 2016|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref>

On 7 December 2017, after missing all of the 2017–18 season up to that point, Ajinça was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing surgery on his right patellar tendon, an injury that typically takes four to six months to recover.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/alexis-ajinca-medical-update-12-7-17|title=Alexis Ajinca Medical Update|work=NBA.com|date=7 December 2017|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref>

On 15 October 2018, Ajinça was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wesley Johnson]].<ref name=clips-trade>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-la-clippers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Complete Trade With New Orleans|work=NBA.com|date=15 October 2018|access-date=15 October 2018}}</ref> He was waived by the Clippers immediately upon being acquired.<ref name="clips-trade" />

===ASVEL (2018–2019)===
On 28 December 2018, Ajinça returned to France and signed with [[ASVEL Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexis AJINÇA renforce LDLC ASVEL|url=https://ldlcasvel.com/alexis-ajinca-renforce-ldlc-asvel|language=FR|date=28 December 2018|website=ldlcasvel.com|access-date=28 December 2018|archive-date=29 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229223107/https://ldlcasvel.com/alexis-ajinca-renforce-ldlc-asvel/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 13 October 2023, Ajinça was hired as an assistant coach by the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Capital City Go-Go Announce 2023-24 Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/capital-city-go-go-announce-2023-24-coaching-staff/n-6022461|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=13 October 2023|access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

On 10 July 2024, Ajinça became an assistant coach for the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Announce Coaching Staff Additions|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-announce-coaching-staff-additions|website=NBA.com|date=10 July 2024|access-date=7 August 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
In September 2013, Ajinça represented the [[France national basketball team|French national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2013]] in Slovenia. He averaged 9.1 points and 7.0 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/playerID_47801.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2013.roundID_8739.teamID_282.html|title=Alexis Ajinca|work=fibaeurope.com|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ajinça and his wife Courtney have two sons, Carter and Caysen.<ref>{{cite web|last=Eichenhofer|first=Jim|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/christmas-special-day-nba-year-its-even-more-memorable-pelicans-alexis-ajinca-john-salmons|title=Christmas is special day for NBA; this year it's even more memorable for Pelicans' Alexis Ajinca, John Salmons|work=NBA.com|date=24 December 2014|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Eichenhofer|first=Jim|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/dad-second-time-month-alexis-ajinca-relishes-joys-fatherhood|title=Alexis Ajinca relishes joys of fatherhood|work=NBA.com|date=9 October 2017|access-date=7 December 2017}}</ref> His cousin, [[Melvin Ajinça]], is a professional basketball player.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bertrande |first1=Arnaud |title=Melvin Ajinça : "Faire mieux que mon cousin" |url=https://www.lequotidiendusport.fr/melvin-ajinca-faire-mieux-que-mon-cousin/ |website=Le Quotidien du Sport |access-date=30 November 2023 |date=26 April 2022 |language=French}}</ref>
